name: Neuroparalytic Keratitis

criteria.description: Presence of corneal anesthesia or hypoesthesia confirmed by esthesiometry
Non-healing corneal epithelial defects or ulceration without infectious etiology
Evidence of trigeminal nerve dysfunction or damage by clinical history or imaging
Exclusion of infectious keratitis by microbiological studies
Poor response to conventional ulcer treatment and improvement with neurotrophic therapies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (corneal anesthesia, corneal ulceration without infection, and trigeminal nerve dysfunction) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of infectious and other causes of corneal ulceration.

pathognomonic.notes: Loss of corneal sensation due to trigeminal nerve impairment
Non-healing corneal ulcers despite standard treatment
Sterile ulcer formation secondary to neurotrophic changes

common.notes: Vision impairment due to corneal damage
Reduced tear production or blink reflex
Despite corneal anesthesia, patients may report discomfort
Light sensitivity due to corneal irritation
Redness of the eye from inflammation

occasional.notes: Swelling of corneal layers secondary to ulceration
Abnormal blood vessel growth into the cornea
Drooping eyelid due to associated nerve dysfunction
Pain may be reduced due to corneal anesthesia
Excessive tearing secondary to ocular surface irritation

rare.notes: Full-thickness corneal defect as a severe complication
Infection due to compromised corneal integrity
Progressive stromal degradation due to nerve dysfunction

laboratory: Negative microbiological cultures from corneal scrapings
Tear film analysis showing reduced neuropeptides
imaging: MRI or CT showing trigeminal nerve pathology or damage
Corneal confocal microscopy demonstrating nerve fiber loss
other: Corneal esthesiometry confirming reduced or absent corneal sensation
Slit-lamp examination revealing epithelial defects and stromal changes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of infectious organisms on culture
Tear film instability without neurotrophic changes

references: Bonini S, Rama P, Olzi D, Lambiase A. Neurotrophic keratitis. Eye (Lond). 2003;17(8):989-995.
Sacchetti M, Lambiase A. Diagnosis and management of neurotrophic keratitis. Clin Ophthalmol. 2014;8:571-579.
Lambiase A, Rama P, Bonini S. Neurotrophic keratitis: clinical presentation and therapeutic approaches. Clin Ophthalmol. 2007;1(3): 255-263.
